Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexGen CyberSecure Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star one to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NexGen CyberSecure's results for the second quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Security Officer; and Casey Wong, VP of Sales.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. NexGen CyberSecure continues to demonstrate leadership in the cybersecurity market. We achieved record bookings in the second quarter, driven by strong demand for our integrated security platform and our expanding global presence. The positive customer feedback about our FalconX platform and the resulting acceleration in XDR adoption is very encouraging.

We are focused on six strategic priorities: gaining market share across core segments like EDR, XDR, SASE, and cloud security; mitigating the impact of currency fluctuations through hedging and pricing strategies; sustaining our high Net Dollar Retention rate through platform expansions; delivering on our full-year revenue and profitability outlook amid rising threats; improving competitive win rates in key bake-offs; and driving expansion within existing large accounts to boost NRR.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. We delivered another quarter of strong financial results. Total revenue for the second quarter was $1.28 billion, representing a 25% increase year-over-year. On a constant currency basis, growth was even stronger at 28.2%, reflecting underlying demand momentum. We saw significant growth in our subscription revenue, which now accounts for 72% of our total revenue. Gross margin expanded to 82%, while operating expenses were controlled at $800 million. Net income was $250 million, resulting in earnings per share of $1.50. We are raising our full-year guidance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial objectives.

As we look at our market share trends, they continue to underscore NexGen CyberSecure's leadership in the rapidly evolving cybersecurity landscape. The global cybersecurity market reached about $52 billion in 2023 per IDC, with projections for 15-18% CAGR through 2028, fueled by ransomware attacks up 37% year-over-year according to Chainalysis, accelerating cloud migrations, and AI-driven threats like sophisticated phishing and deepfakes. In our core segments—Endpoint Detection and Response, Extended Detection and Response, Secure Access Service Edge, and Cloud Workload Protection—we expanded market share by 120 basis points year-over-year, from 4.1% in Q2 2023 to 5.3% in Q2 2024, based on Gartner Magic Quadrant metrics and our internal win/loss data. This outpaces the market and positions us ahead of peers. While CrowdStrike holds 12.8% in EDR, we've gained from legacy players like Symantec, now at 8.2% from 9.7%, capturing 22% of their displaced EDR deals this quarter.

In EDR and XDR, we gained 280 basis points to 6.8% share, thanks to FalconX's AI-native behavioral analytics and 99.7% zero-day detection per MITRE ATT&CK, winning 68% against SentinelOne and Microsoft Defender, especially in mid-market with our sub-50ms query latency. XDR upsells drove $145 million in ARR, up 42% year-over-year, with net retention at 118%. In SASE and Zero Trust, share rose 190 basis points to 4.9%, powered by PrismaEdge integrating ZTNA, SWG, and CASB with quantum-resistant encryption. We displaced Zscaler in 14% of deals, aided by our Auto-Remediation Engine automating 85% of policy violations post-Okta incidents. Cloud security shone with 7.2% share, up 350 basis points, outgrowing Wiz and Orca in CNAPP via ShieldCloud's agentless scanning covering 98% of AWS, Azure, and GCP, including a $28 million ACV hyperscaler win amid 45% cloud misconfig surges per Palo Alto's Unit 42.

Regionally, North America at 65% of revenue holds 8.1% share, up from 6.9%, with FedRAMP High aiding federal wins and 25% capture of ransomware recovery budgets from Check Point. EMEA at 18% gained 210 basis points to 4.2% via GDPR compliance in Nexus SIEM, strong in UK G-Cloud and German BSI. APAC at 12% exploded 410 basis points to 3.1% amid APTs like Salt Typhoon, with Tencent Cloud adding $42 million pipeline targeting 5% by FY25. LATAM at 5% rose 150 basis points to 1.8% on Brazil's LGPD.

These gains come from innovation with $320 million Q2 R&D yielding GenAI Threat Hunter cutting MTTR 67% and blockchain supply chain monitoring; go-to-market via AWS and Cisco channels at 52% of new logos, 41% win rates rising to 65% in greenfield XDR; and M&A like ThreatMesh adding 80 basis points in CWP. Tailwinds include SEC rules and EU NIS2, offset by firewall pricing and forex risks, but 125% gross margins and 92% retention provide buffer. We guide 100-150 basis points H2 expansion to 6% overall.

Before segments, a note on currency fluctuations impacting revenue. With 45% from international markets serving 12,000 customers via Nexus Endpoint Protection, ThreatShield XDR, and SecureAccess SASE, FX headwinds dragged reported growth. Q2's $24.7 million negative impact equaled 1.9 points headwind, better than Q1's $31.2 million, from USD up 12% against key currencies amid Fed hikes to 525-550 bps versus ECB's 375 bps and weak yen.

Americas at 55% or $704 million grew 32% reported matching constant currency, from AWS/Azure XDR and CISA mandates. EMEA at 25% or $320 million took $15.4 million hit from 14% EUR and 8% GBP drops, reported 18% vs. 24% constant, yet ARR up 45% on NATO defenses and DAX expansions. APAC at 15% or $192 million had $7.2 million drag from JPY 18% and AUD 9% falls, 22% vs. 27% constant, offset by Australia's Essential Eight and Singapore levies. Rest of World at 5% or $64 million saw minor $2.1 million volatility but 40% growth.

Year-to-date FX shaved $55.9 million, mostly EMEA/APAC. Subscriptions diluted 1.4% vs. 2.8% services. Hedging covers 75% FY exposure up from 60%, dynamic pricing in Nexus CPQ, APAC diversification via Tencent, USD pricing in EMEA, and SaaS shift reduce noise. Constant currency shows durability amid 15% threat rise per Mandiant.

Our Net Dollar Retention rate for trailing 12 months ended Q2 hit 118%, up 600 basis points from 112% and 11th straight sequential gain, matching CrowdStrike and ahead of Palo Alto, with $1M+ ARR cohort at 125%. Gross retention at 96% with <2% expansionary churn, NPS 68 on Clop responses. Expansion at 123% from 45% upsells, 35% cross-sells, 20% seats, layering ZTNA/CWP on EDR.

Platformization has 70% top 500 on 3+ modules up from 55% post-Log4j/MOVEit, GenAI module $45 million expansion ARR. CyberGuard Sentinel ML analytics integrated with Splunk/Elastic cut MTTR 40% for Fortune 50. North America 120% NDR on CISA/hyperscalers; EMEA 115% on NIS2/DLP; APAC 128% on LockBit/CSPM. Customer Success Pods unlocked $220 million YTD expansions, guiding 117-122% FY25 with Quantum-Resistant suite.

For full-year outlook ending January 2025, revenue $3.05-3.15 billion, 22-26% growth from $2.50 billion, up from prior $2.95-3.05 billion on subscriptions/SASE-XDR. Subscriptions $2.65-2.75 billion, 25-29%; services $400-450 million, 15-23%. ARR $2.40 billion Q2-end, 125%+ expansion, $1.2 million Q3 new ACV. Americas $2.15-2.20 billion +24%; EMEA $600-650 million +28%; APAC $300 million +18%.

SecureXDR 2.0 added $250 million pipeline, EdgeDefend acquisition $450 million bolsters endpoints. Non-GAAP op margin 28-30% from 82% subs margins, sales 65% revenue; EPS $4.85-5.05. FCF $950 million-1.0 billion. Risks: sales cycles, budgets, FX; visibility from 3.5x book-to-bill, $1.2 billion RPO.

Competitive win rates at 48% Q2, up 450 bps sequential/620 bps YoY, above 35-40% industry per IDC, from Unified Threat Platform. Vs. CrowdStrike 55% on 127 EDR deals, HyperShield 25% fewer false positives. Cloud vs. Zscaler 62% on 89, sub-50ms ZTE. Legacy 68%, Palo Alto 51% CWPP. Microsoft 45%. Large deals 52%, endpoint/XDR 53%, SASE 46%. Americas 50%, EMEA 55%, APAC 42%. R&D $185 million H1: GenAI +15% POCs, quantum, OT/IoT 65%. Q3 48-50%.

Expansion in large accounts >$1M ACV, 65% ARR $2.8 billion, grew 28% YoY to $156 million, NRR 128% up 500 bps. Seats 42%, upsells 35%, extensions 23%; avg ACV $4.96 million. 72% on 3+ modules. ZTA/GenAI 41% expansions, MTTD -65%; financials $18 million ARR. RaaS/Deception; hyperscaler $12.5 million. CNAPP 35% YoY. NA 32%, EMEA 25%, APAC 19%. CSO 94% renewals, $320 million Q4 pipe, AWS co-sell 28%. Guide 30-35% growth contribution, 125-130% NRR.

We are reiterating our full-year guidance and remain confident.

Taylor Kim: Thank you, Jordan. Our engineering team is laser-focused on innovation and delivering cutting-edge security solutions. We are leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance our threat detection and response capabilities. Key areas of focus include advancing GenAI Threat Hunter reducing MTTR by 67%, ShieldCloud agentless multi-cloud scanning, and CyberGuard Sentinel for behavioral analytics integrating with SIEMs like Splunk, alongside quantum-resistant encryption and autonomous SOAR to counter polymorphic malware and APTs.

Morgan Patel: Security remains our top priority. We are constantly monitoring the threat landscape—from ransomware surges like Conti and LockBit to state-sponsored APTs and supply chain risks like SolarWinds—and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and infrastructure, with FedRAMP High, GDPR compliance, and proactive red-teaming ensuring resilience.

Casey Wong: Thank you. We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is executing well, with 41% overall win rates and channel partnerships like AWS Marketplace and Cisco contributing 52% new logos, expanding reach in hyperscalers, financials, and critical infrastructure while targeting 65% greenfield XDR wins.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the Q&A session. First question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Chen: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Can you elaborate on the market share gains in cloud security and how that ties to competitive dynamics?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Mike. Our 350 basis point gain to 7.2% in cloud security stems from ShieldCloud's 98% multi-cloud coverage outpacing Wiz and Orca in CNAPP, securing hyperscaler deals like the $28 million ACV win. Competitively, we won 51% against Palo Alto Prisma Cloud via eBPF kernel introspection for Kubernetes, aligning with 45% misconfig surges and vendor consolidation trends.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Patel: Great, thanks. On FX headwinds, how are you mitigating ongoing exposure and what’s the constant currency view for H2?

Jordan Lee: Lisa, thanks. FX dragged $24.7 million Q2, but hedging 75% FY exposure via forwards/options at favorable rates like EUR/USD 1.12, dynamic CPQ pricing for 5-10% swings, USD contracts in EMEA, and SaaS billing alignment mitigate. H2 expects $40-50 million drag at consensus rates, potentially $60 million if USD +5%, but constant currency growth holds 26-28% on subscription durability.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Singh with JPMorgan.

Raj Singh: Thanks for taking my question. Impressive NDR—curious about drivers in APAC and large account expansions there.

Taylor Kim: Raj, our 128% APAC NDR and 19% large account growth reflect LockBit ransomware and Lazarus campaigns driving CSPM cross-sells to 60% base, plus Singapore sovereign cloud integrations. Technical edge from sensor fusion and GenAI modules, with expansions like $10 million+ ACVs in Australia/Japan, bolstered by 35% seat growth.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Barclays.

Emily Rodriguez: Hi, team. Thoughts on competitive win rates versus CrowdStrike and Palo Alto, and sustainability?

Morgan Patel: Emily, our 55% vs. CrowdStrike on 127 EDR deals from HyperShield's lower false positives and non-Windows strength, and 51% vs. Palo Alto CWPP leverage MITRE-validated efficacy and NIS2 tailwinds. Sustainability from R&D like GenAI hunting +15% POCs and platformization—70% multi-module wins—positions us for 48-50% Q3 amid consolidation.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for cybersecurity solutions. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
